independent_mathematical_checks: Finite chart bumps have compact support within each ordinary/half-ball domain. Positive scalar block recovers chart coordinates, proving finite-dimensional embedding without separability or partition-of-unity choices.

Chart-ratio maps are defined on open O_i. Clamping the last coordinate to max(0,x_n) decreases norm, fixes the half-ball, and hence fixes all M points in O_i. Compact K_i permit positive delta neighborhoods with compact support contained in O_i.

At the inductive step, for x in M intersect S_j the old controlled property gives an ambient neighborhood where all defined old values lie in V_j. Outside closed S_j an ambient neighborhood misses it. Union of all admissible opens contains M and retains the pointwise containment; no pointwise neighborhood selector is used.

Blending is continuous at a=0,b>0 because the old chart vector is uniformly bounded and its coefficient tends to zero. At b=0,a>0, either S_j is locally absent or the old value lies in V_j and continuity supplies valid chart coordinates.

Controlledness persists even at M points not in D_j: both defined old values and q_j values lie in a common arbitrarily small convex chart neighborhood, including half-ball boundary points. All endpoint cases stay in it. Finite induction yields identity on M and open final domain containing M.

Uniform epsilon neighborhood and one sufficiently fine fixed grid give finitely many cubes meeting bounded M. Every cube lies inside the retraction domain by its diameter, and all faces form a finite cubical CW complex. No nearest-point selection, infinite cell extension, manifold triangulation, homotopy-finite CW equivalence or Wall obstruction assertion is used.
Empty manifolds choose empty neighborhood/complex; compact zero-manifolds are finite and handled separately. All noncanonical data selected are a finite list, valid in ZF.
